    AI Overview
    The Artemis II Orion capsule safely splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET. The successful, parachute-assisted landing concluded a historic 10-day mission around the moon, with the crew safely returning home for recovery by U.S. Navy and NASA teams. 
     
    • Final Moments: The capsule re-entered Earth's atmosphere at roughly
      , enduring intense heat before utilizing, in order, drogue chutes and then three main parachutes to slow down to about
      for the final splashdown.
    • Splashdown & Recovery: Following the splashdown, inflatable bags were deployed to ensure the capsule remained upright. Recovery crews were on standby, aiming to get the crew out of the capsule within approximately two hours.
    • Mission Significance: This mission serves as a critical test for NASA's Artemis program, ensuring systems are safe for future moon landings. 
    Crew Members: 
    • Reid Wiseman
    • Victor Glover
    • Christina Koch
    • Jeremy Hansen 
    The successful return prepares the way for future Artemis missions, including the planned lunar landing in upcoming years.
